paragraphs.text: This holy abstinence of the priests in matter of mourning, marriage, &c., figured the transcendent holiness of Christ: the devils could call him that Holy One of God. {Mar 1:24} It taught also both ministers and people, who are "a kingdom of priests"; (1.) Well to govern their passions, and to be patterns of patience; (2.) Ever to keep such a Sabbath of spirit, that by no dead works, or persons dead in trespasses and sins, they be hindered in the discharge of their duties of either calling.
paragraphs.anchor: There shall none be defiled for the dead.

paragraphs.text: The high priest might not for any of these, {Lev 21:10-11} nor might Eleazar and Ithamar for their dead brethren Nadab and Abihu, {Lev 10:6} because in that case, mourning might have seemed murmuring.

What! and not for his wife? Yes surely, though she be not mentioned, because she is nearer than either daughter or sister. See Eze 24:16. He was a priest, but that was an exempt case, an exception from what was ordinarily done.
A vir gregis; all whose actions were exemplary, and have not an impulsive only, but a compulsive power and property. "Why compellest thou the Gentiles?" {Gal 2:14} His example was a compulsion.

So Lev 19:27. Howbeit in humiliation for sin the Lord God of hosts called them all, both priests and people, to weeping and mourning, {Joe 2:17} yea to baldness and sackcloth. {Isa 22:12} Here we cannot easily overdo.
Heb., Holiness, i.e. all holy, even as holiness itself, merely spiritual.
Not do anything unworthy the majesty of the ministry: but suffer the dead to bury their dead. {Mat 8:22}
paragraphs.anchor: Not profane the name of their God.

paragraphs.text: Lest their function be disgraced. That which Hosea was commanded to do against this prohibition {Hos 1:2} was but visional.
paragraphs.anchor: They shall not take a wife.

paragraphs.text: Deflowered, ravished.
Because of evil report.
i.e., Thou, Moses, shalt command him to be sanctified, as Exo 19:10.
A peculiar plague, to show the hatefulness of the sin.
paragraphs.anchor: She shall be burnt with fire.

paragraphs.text: So neither doth the Mufti among the Turks, nor the Pope of Rome uncover to any man: but this is their pride and stateliness.
But appear impassionate, as it were, and more than a man.
Noting thereby that Christ, now risen, is crowned with glory and honour; {Heb 2:7 Zec 6:12} and so shall we with him. {Heb 2:9-10 1Co 15:47-49}
paragraphs.anchor: For the crown of the anointing.

paragraphs.text: Such is Christ’s wife, {2Co 11:1-33: 2Ki 14:4 Mat 25:1-13} not giving her love, or his worship to any other.
A Jewess of any tribe. {Eze 44:22 2Ch 22:11}
Disable them for the priesthood by marrying such a wife as was forbidden him.
Christ was without blemish: so should all the saints be, but especially ministers, of whom it should be said as of Absalom, that from top to toe there was no blemish in him. {2Sa 14:25}

Lest his ministry be slighted for his personal defects and deformities: how much more for his ignorance, envy, indirect aims, uneven walking, injudiciousness, unheavenly mindedness, &c., purported by these bodily imperfections?
In the hands, the Hebrews say, there might be seven blemishes.
By a mixture of the humours there, or otherwise; when that little man {a} in the eye, as the Hebrews call the apple thereof, acteth not his part aright.
{a} Ishon
So might not the unclean priests. {Lev 22:3} Our involuntary weaknesses shall not debar us from benefit by Christ.
By my presence, and services there performed.
paragraphs.anchor: For I the Lord do sanctify them.

paragraphs.text: Who were to see that these things were thus done.
